kid.question: What will the Lord use to make Zion’s borders beautiful?

options.text: Agates for Zion’s windows
Carbuncles for Zion’s gates
Gold on Zion’s walls
Pleasant and precious stones

kid.explanation: Isaiah 54:12 supports this answer: Isaiah describes jeweled gates, windows, and borders..

kid.question: Who will teach Zion’s children?

options.text: The watchmen of Jerusalem
The rulers of the nations
The Lord
The priests of Babylon

kid.explanation: Isaiah 54:13 states this teaching: The Lord.

kid.question: What will be far from Zion when she is established in righteousness?

options.text: Famine and captivity
Oppression and terror
Fear and shame
Weapons and accusations

kid.explanation: Isaiah 54:14 states this teaching: Oppression and terror.

kid.question: What kind of outcome does the Lord promise regarding weapons formed against His servants?

options.text: No weapon formed against them will prosper
Those weapons will establish Zion
The servants will surrender to their enemies
The weapons will replace the Lord’s covenant

kid.explanation: Isaiah 54:17 states this teaching: No weapon formed against them will prosper.

kid.question: Who is invited to come to the waters?

options.text: What is good and truly nourishing from the Lord
Life-giving blessings are offered freely to those who listen
Nations unfamiliar with Israel will be drawn to the Lord
Everyone who thirsts

kid.explanation: Isaiah 55:1 supports this answer: Isaiah calls every thirsty person to come..

kid.question: What should people seek instead of what cannot satisfy?

options.text: Life-giving blessings are offered freely to those who listen
Nations unfamiliar with Israel will be drawn to the Lord
What is good and truly nourishing from the Lord
Everyone who thirsts

kid.explanation: Isaiah 55:2 supports this answer: Isaiah invites them to listen and receive what satisfies..

kid.question: What should people do while the Lord is near?

options.text: Forsaking sinful ways and thoughts, then returning to the Lord
Seek Him and call upon Him
The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons
As the heavens are higher than the earth

kid.explanation: Isaiah 55:6 supports this answer: Isaiah tells them to seek the Lord and call on Him..

kid.question: What happens when the wicked return to the Lord?

options.text: The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons
Seek Him and call upon Him
As the heavens are higher than the earth
Forsaking sinful ways and thoughts, then returning to the Lord

kid.explanation: Isaiah 55:7 supports this answer: Isaiah promises mercy and abundant pardon..

kid.question: How much higher are the Lord’s ways than ours?

options.text: Seek Him and call upon Him
The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons
Forsaking sinful ways and thoughts, then returning to the Lord
As the heavens are higher than the earth

kid.explanation: Isaiah 55:9 supports this answer: Isaiah uses the height of heaven to describe the difference..

kid.question: How will the people go out?

options.text: Joy, peace, and flourishing growth replacing thorn and brier
God’s speech fulfills its intended work just as rain produces earthly yield
With joy and be led in peace
As rain nourishes earth, His word accomplishes the purpose for which He sends it

kid.explanation: Isaiah 55:12 supports this answer: The verse promises joy and peace..

high-school.question: What kind of restoration is pictured by jeweled walls and children taught by God?

options.text: The Lord
Oppression and terror
A beautiful, peaceful community shaped by divine instruction
Pleasant and precious stones

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 54:12-13 supports this answer: The passage joins a rebuilt city with children taught of the Lord..

high-school.question: On what basis does Isaiah promise safety from weapons and accusation?

options.text: Oppression and terror
The servants’ righteousness comes from the Lord
Pleasant and precious stones
The Lord

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 54:14-17 supports this answer: The promise ends by attributing their righteousness to God..

high-school.question: What does the image of buying food without money teach about the Lord’s invitation?

options.text: Life-giving blessings are offered freely to those who listen
Everyone who thirsts
What is good and truly nourishing from the Lord
Nations unfamiliar with Israel will be drawn to the Lord

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 55:1-2 supports this answer: The invitation is without price and calls people to what satisfies..

high-school.question: What does the everlasting covenant make possible beyond Israel?

options.text: Everyone who thirsts
What is good and truly nourishing from the Lord
Life-giving blessings are offered freely to those who listen
Nations unfamiliar with Israel will be drawn to the Lord

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 55:3-5 supports this answer: Isaiah says unknown nations will run to them because of God..

high-school.question: What two changes accompany the promise of pardon?

options.text: The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons
As the heavens are higher than the earth
Forsaking sinful ways and thoughts, then returning to the Lord
Seek Him and call upon Him

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 55:6-7 supports this answer: Isaiah connects turning from sin with receiving mercy..

high-school.question: Why should people avoid measuring the Lord’s choices only by their own?

options.text: As the heavens are higher than the earth
His thoughts and ways exceed theirs as heaven exceeds earth
Seek Him and call upon Him
The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 55:8-9 supports this answer: The verses state the comparison directly..

high-school.question: How does rain illustrate the effect of the Lord’s word?

options.text: As rain nourishes earth, His word accomplishes the purpose for which He sends it
Rain returns to heaven without nourishing the earth
God’s word may fail to accomplish its purpose
The Lord’s word is only a temporary source of food

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 55:10-11 states this teaching: As rain nourishes earth, His word accomplishes the purpose for which He sends it.

high-school.question: How does Isaiah describe the people’s joyful departure?

options.text: With joy and be led in peace
As rain nourishes earth, His word accomplishes the purpose for which He sends it
God’s speech fulfills its intended work just as rain produces earthly yield
Joy, peace, and flourishing growth replacing thorn and brier

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 55:12 describes this joyful departure: They go out with joy and peace as creation sings.

high-school.question: How does Isaiah distinguish hostile gathering from the Lord’s purpose?

options.text: The Lord
Oppression and terror
Opponents may gather, but their attack will not prevail
Pleasant and precious stones

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 54:15-17 supports this answer: The Lord says gatherings against Zion are not from Him and weapons fail..

high-school.question: Why does “seek” belong with “return” in Isaiah’s invitation?

options.text: As the heavens are higher than the earth
The invitation calls both the near and the straying person back to God’s mercy
Seek Him and call upon Him
The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons

high-school.explanation: Isaiah 55:6-7 supports this answer: The passage couples seeking God with forsaking a way and returning..

expert.question: What relationship between civic beauty and spiritual life does Isaiah present?

The renewed city’s splendor accompanies children’s instruction by the Lord
Pleasant and precious stones
The Lord

expert.explanation: Isaiah 54:12-13 supports this answer: The architectural imagery is followed by divine teaching and peace..

options.text: Their vindication and righteousness belong to the Lord
Pleasant and precious stones
The Lord
Oppression and terror

expert.explanation: Isaiah 54:14-17 supports this answer: Isaiah concludes that their righteousness is from Him..

expert.question: How does the no-price feast challenge the logic of labor and exchange?

options.text: Everyone who thirsts
What is good and truly nourishing from the Lord
Life-giving blessings are offered freely to those who listen
True satisfaction comes by heeding God rather than spending on what is not bread

expert.explanation: Isaiah 55:1-2 supports this answer: Isaiah contrasts costly futility with free nourishment..

expert.question: How does the Davidic covenant expand the audience of the promise?

options.text: What is good and truly nourishing from the Lord
Life-giving blessings are offered freely to those who listen
The Lord’s covenant witness becomes a draw for nations that did not know Israel
Everyone who thirsts

expert.explanation: Isaiah 55:3-5 supports this answer: The passage moves from the sure mercies of David to unfamiliar nations..

expert.question: What structure links human repentance with divine pardon?

options.text: As the heavens are higher than the earth
Forsaking both conduct and thought opens into a return met by abundant mercy
Seek Him and call upon Him
The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons

expert.explanation: Isaiah 55:6-7 supports this answer: Isaiah names the inward and outward turn before promising pardon..

expert.question: What function does the heaven-earth comparison serve?

options.text: It cautions that divine judgment and mercy cannot be reduced to human scale
Seek Him and call upon Him
The Lord has mercy and abundantly pardons
As the heavens are higher than the earth

expert.explanation: Isaiah 55:8-9 supports this answer: The Lord’s higher ways explain why His thoughts differ from ours..

expert.question: What does the rain analogy claim about the efficacy of revelation?

options.text: The rain’s return is more certain than the Lord’s word
Revelation succeeds only when it is repeated by people
The word serves mainly as a symbol of nourishment
God’s speech fulfills its intended work just as rain produces earthly yield

expert.explanation: Isaiah 55:10-11 states this teaching: God’s speech fulfills its intended work just as rain produces earthly yield.

expert.question: How does creation participate in the people’s return?

options.text: As rain nourishes earth, His word accomplishes the purpose for which He sends it
Joy, peace, and flourishing growth replacing thorn and brier
Mountains and trees poetically join their joyful, peaceful procession
With joy and be led in peace

expert.explanation: Isaiah 55:12 describes this joyful departure: Mountains, hills, and trees poetically join their joyful procession.

expert.question: What distinction does Isaiah draw between divine creation and hostile action?

options.text: Oppression and terror
God creates tools and agents, yet hostile weapons cannot overturn His servants’ inheritance
Pleasant and precious stones
The Lord

expert.explanation: Isaiah 54:15-17 supports this answer: The Lord’s creative power precedes the promise that weapons will fail..

expert.question: How do thirst, listening, and covenant form a progression?

options.text: The needy are invited to receive freely, heed God, and enter lasting covenant life
Everyone who thirsts
What is good and truly nourishing from the Lord
Life-giving blessings are offered freely to those who listen

expert.explanation: Isaiah 55:1-3 supports this answer: The call to the waters leads into hearing and the everlasting covenant..
